title: Chard, smoked haddock and new potato frittata

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food a grandparent would keep: potatoes, smoked haddock, milk, eggs, chard, spring onions, chives, Cheddar and salad leaves.

supermarket.reason: Smoked haddock, chard, new potatoes and the rest are everyday items at a mainstream UK supermarket at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only saucepans, an ovenproof frying pan, a bowl, a whisk and the grill, and the technique suits a confident beginner.

works.reason: Eight eggs with 400g potatoes, 300g haddock and 250g chard in a 26cm pan gives a well-filled frittata for four, and setting it on the hob then finishing under the grill is sound.

honest_times.reason: Poaching the haddock and preparing the chard overlap with the potato boil, so 25 minutes hands-on and about 40 minutes in total is believable.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and the cod in the tip is on the June list.

seasonal_feel.reason: Early June chard and new potatoes make up the body of the dish, and a warm frittata with salad suits a June lunch.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, practical British English, including a useful note on going easy with the salt because the haddock is already salty.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling, balanced lunch of eggs, fish, greens and potatoes with salad on the side.
